Literature guard: the small-fiber-and-sleep comorbidity data are idiopathic-small-fiber-neuropathy-population scoped; the erythromelalgia-specific sleep literature records sleep disruption narratively without EM-specific prevalence, so the insomnia edge is written under an explicit population-scope guard.
governanceNotes: D1 batch 30 (2026-09-23): two bounded associations authored - an episcleritis-to-scleritis association anchored on the Friberg 2014 burden survey (insomnia 37%, the most common comorbidity of painful small-fiber neuropathy, the class erythromelalgia belongs to) and an episcleritis-to-keratitis association from the same survey and the Mantyh 2017 Mayo Clinic cohort documenting small-fiber structural pathology in erythromelalgia; the population-scope guard (SFN-population data, not EM-specific prevalence) is recorded on both edges.

The erythromelalgia identity is a distinct entity under the ME-41 barrier language (recorded at the acrocyanosis deferral), and these are its first outgoing edges; no ulceration or amputation edge is authored because the catalog's wound and amputation identities carry diabetic/neuropathic-ulcer-scoped evidence and erythromelalgia-specific outcome data are case-series class without denominators - recorded as an evidence gap rather than an edge.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: In the Friberg 2014 burden survey of 100 painful idiopathic small-fiber neuropathy patients, sleep disturbance/insomnia was the most common comorbidity at 37.0% and the sleep index (45.1/100) and pain interference (5.0/10) worsened significantly with pain severity (all p < 0.002); erythromelalgia belongs to this small-fiber pain-disorder class, and the Caldito 2024 review documents recurrent bouts of burning pain and sleep disruption as characteristic of the condition.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the quantified comorbidity prevalence is SFN-population scoped rather than erythromelalgia-specific, reverse direction is live (poor sleep lowers pain thresholds and amplifies burning episodes), and insomnia must meet documented diagnostic criteria rather than self-report.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized nocturnal-pain sleep-fragmentation pathway: erythromelalgia attacks are provoked by heat and characteristically worsen at night under bedding warmth, so recurrent nocturnal burning, heat-escape behaviors (uncovering feet, walking cold floors, cooling soaks), and anticipatory anxiety fragment sleep onset and maintenance; chronic fragmentation produces the documented insomnia phenotype. Individual attribution requires documented sleep disturbance with compatible chronology against the pain diary.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The comorbidity quantification is drawn from the broader painful-SFN population and applied to erythromelalgia by class membership; reverse direction and shared mood-anxiety drivers are live, and insomnia must be documented by validated criteria with a pain-compatible chronology; no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented erythromelalgia (Mayo criteria or neurologist diagnosis) with attack diary; documented insomnia by validated instrument (ISI or PSG) with chronology relative to attacks; exclusion of primary insomnia, restless legs, sleep-disordered breathing, and stimulant or medication effects; sleep-medicine assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Restless legs syndrome or periodic limb movement disorder
Stimulant, corticosteroid, or antidepressant medication effects
Independent anxiety or depressive disorder driving insomnia

evidenceGaps: Documented erythromelalgia (Mayo criteria or neurologist diagnosis) with attack diary; documented insomnia by validated instrument (ISI or PSG) with chronology relative to attacks; exclusion of primary insomnia, restless legs, sleep-disordered breathing, and stimulant or medication effects; sleep-medicine assessment of the individual relationship
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: the sleep comorbidity of painful small-fiber disorders is survey-quantified, but the evidence is population-scoped, the reverse direction is live, and erythromelalgia-specific sleep data remain narrative; no causation is forced.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Erythromelalgia is characterized in the JAAD two-part review as a rare, underrecognized, difficult-to-treat pain disorder with disabling extremity erythema and burning (Caldito 2024 Part I), and the Mantyh 2017 Mayo Clinic cohort documents small-fiber structural pathology in a large share of consecutive patients, aligning the condition with the chronic-neuropathic-pain spectrum the unexplained-chronic-pain identity captures.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The mapping does not assert causation: the chronic pain is the disease's own defining presentation rather than a downstream outcome, so the edge is an association-of-co-occurrence for case-matching purposes only; individual claims require documented erythromelalgia plus separately documented chronic pain attribution and exclusion of other pain generators.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized small-fiber central-sensitization pathway: constitutive Nav1.7 gain-of-function or structural small-fiber loss produces persistent C-fiber ectopic firing and central sensitization, converting episodic burning into continuous pain with allodynia and mechanical hyperalgesia between attacks; the target identity is used for case-matching and the pathway records the mechanism discussed in the literature rather than an individual claim.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The pain is constitutive of the erythromelalgia identity, so this edge asserts no separate disease process; the unexplained-chronic-pain identity requires documented pain exceeding 3 months without a fully explaining alternative, competing pain generators must be excluded, and the sensitization pathway is hypothesis-class; no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented erythromelalgia diagnosis; documented chronic pain by validated instruments with functional impact; exclusion of radiculopathy, neuropathy of other cause, CRPS, and vascular claudication as the pain driver; pain-specialty assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Lumbar radiculopathy or peripheral neuropathy of another etiology
Peripheral arterial disease with claudication or critical ischemia
Fibromyalgia or centralized pain of independent origin

evidenceGaps: Documented erythromelalgia diagnosis; documented chronic pain by validated instruments with functional impact; exclusion of radiculopathy, neuropathy of other cause, CRPS, and vascular claudication as the pain driver; pain-specialty assessment of the individual relationship
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: the chronic-pain burden is the defining feature of the disease and the co-occurrence association serves case-matching; because the pain is constitutive rather than downstream, no causal claim is possible and none is asserted.
